explain.say: See these two bars? About 10 percent of Africa was under European rule in 1870. By 1914 it was about 90 percent. That rush is called the Scramble for Africa. How many times bigger is the second bar?

But Africans resisted. In 1896 at Adwa, Ethiopia's army, led by Emperor Menelik the Second and Empress Taytu, defeated Italy. Strong work today! Wow: by 1914 only Ethiopia and Liberia were still independent, and Adwa is celebrated every year.

faq.q: How much of Africa did Europe rule in 1870?
faq.a: Only about a tenth, mostly coastal areas like parts of Algeria, southern Africa and trading posts in West Africa. Most land was ruled by African states and peoples.

A meeting in Berlin from November 1884 to February 1885, called by German chancellor Otto von Bismarck. Fourteen countries, mostly European, plus the USA and the Ottoman Empire, set rules for claiming Africa. No Africans took part.
asks: Who went to the Berlin Conference?

faq.q: What happened in the Congo Free State?
faq.a: King Leopold II of Belgium ruled the Congo as his personal property from 1885 to 1908. Forced labour to collect rubber, with brutal punishments, led to millions of deaths. International outcry forced Belgium to take it over.
asks: What did King Leopold do in the Congo?

faq.q: What was the Battle of Adwa?
faq.a: On 1 March 1896, Ethiopian forces under Emperor Menelik II defeated an invading Italian army near Adwa. It kept Ethiopia independent and became a proud symbol for Africans everywhere.

For raw materials like rubber, gold and cotton, for new markets, because of rivalry between European nations, and because of beliefs, now rejected, that Europeans had a right to rule others. New guns and medicines like quinine made conquest easier.
asks: What was the Scramble for Africa?

facts: The Berlin Conference ran from November 1884 to February 1885.
Ethiopia defeated Italy at the Battle of Adwa on 1 March 1896.
By 1914 only Ethiopia and Liberia in Africa were independent of European rule.
